Checking costs nothing and keeps the hand, so it is a call priced at zero: it risks nothing and still holds a share of what is already in the middle. That share is what folding gives up, which is why a free check is never worse than a fold.

EV(fold) = 0 chips. Folding is the baseline every other action is measured against: it costs nothing further and risks nothing further. Everything already in the pot is spent either way, so folding is the zero point every other action is measured against.

EV(bet) = f x pot + (1 - f) x [ e x (pot + 2b) - b ] = 0.35 x 30 + 0.65 x [ 0.3509 x (30 + 2 x 10) - 10 ] = 10.5 + 4.91 = 15.41 chips. Risks 10 to win 30. A caller needs 20% equity to break even, and as a pure bluff it would have to work 25% of the time. For bluffs of this size not to print automatically, the player facing it has to continue with 75% of their range.

EV(bet) = f x pot + (1 - f) x [ e x (pot + 2b) - b ] = 0.35 x 30 + 0.65 x [ 0.3509 x (30 + 2 x 22) - 22 ] = 10.5 + 2.58 = 13.08 chips. Risks 22 to win 30. A caller needs 29.7% equity to break even, and as a pure bluff it would have to work 42.3% of the time. For bluffs of this size not to print automatically, the player facing it has to continue with 57.7% of their range.

EV(bet) = f x pot + (1 - f) x [ e x (pot + 2b) - b ] = 0.35 x 30 + 0.65 x [ 0.3509 x (30 + 2 x 990) - 990 ] = 10.5 + (-185) = -174.5 chips. Risks 990 to win 30. A caller needs 49.3% equity to break even, and as a pure bluff it would have to work 97.1% of the time. For bluffs of this size not to print automatically, the player facing it has to continue with 2.9% of their range. Betting this is your whole stack, so it is also an all-in.

suggestion.reason: Bet comes out marginally ahead here, but only just — treat this as close to indifferent rather than as a recommendation.
whatWouldChangeIt: This assumes the line wins uncontested 35% of the time. An opponent who folds less often makes it worse.
Being raised is not modelled here, so treat the figure as optimistic.
The gap to the next-best action is only 2.3 units, well under a big blind — this is close to indifferent.

stackContext.explanation: Yours is the shorter stack: you have 990 and the deepest opponent has 990, so at most 990 can change hands. You can neither win nor lose more than you brought to the hand. With 2 opponents each one has its own effective stack, the smaller of yours and theirs. 990 is the largest of them, so it is the most that can move against any single player and not the most you can lose across all of them. SPR = effective stack / pot = 990 / 30 = 33. There are 33 pots behind, which is the "very-high" band. Almost all of the money is still behind. The pot in front of you is small compared with what can still go in, so the cost of a later error dwarfs what is at stake right now. SPR describes the shape of the decision, not the answer to it: your hand, their range and position all still apply.

assumptions: The hand is played to the river with no further betting — this is raw equity, not the value of the spot.
You hold exactly Th2d.
Seat 1 holds any of 231 combinations from "22+, A2s+, K9s+, QTs+, JTs, A9o+, KTo+, QJo", each equally likely.
Seat 2 holds any of 231 combinations from "22+, A2s+, K9s+, QTs+, JTs, A9o+, KTo+, QJo", each equally likely.
Every hand in a range is weighted equally. Real opponents do not play every hand in a range the same way, so treat this as the range assumption, not a prediction.
Computed by enumerating every remaining board — there is no sampling error.
Bet and raise figures assume the line wins uncontested 35% of the time. That is an input you can change, not something measured.
A half-pot bet of 15 is already break-even or better here purely on the equity you have when called — it does not need to win uncontested at all.
Expected values are measured against folding, which is treated as zero. Chips already in the pot are spent either way.

uncertainty.summary: Computed exactly by enumerating every remaining board (1,935,948 run-outs). There is no sampling error.
limitations: This is raw equity: the hand is treated as running to the river with no further betting. Real hands have more streets and more decisions.
Every hand in the opponent range is weighted equally. Real opponents do not play every hand in a range the same way.
Against several opponents the analysis assumes all of them see the river, which overstates your risk when some would fold.
No implied odds, reverse implied odds or future-street play are modelled.

teachingNotes: At an SPR of 33.0 there is a lot of money left behind, so hands that can keep improving are worth more than their current strength suggests.
